 Search “Tantara” Explained: Song Hye-kyo & Gong Yoo’s Highly Anticipated Netflix K-Drama
 Disha Paul 7 hours ago 5 min read Song Hye-kyo and Gong Yoo chase their dreams in Tantara , Netflix’s highly anticipated period drama set in Korea’s entertainment industry from the 1960s to the 1980s. Premieres December 11, 2026. (Netflix) Netflix has finally revealed when fans can watch Tantara , one of its most anticipated Korean dramas of 2026. Starring Song Hye-kyo and Gong Yoo , the upcoming series has set its premiere for December 11, giving viewers a confirmed date to look forward to. 
 Previously introduced internationally under the working title Show Business , Tantara  takes viewers into South Korea’s entertainment industry from the 1960s through the 1980s. Instead of focusing on the glamorous lives of established celebrities, the story follows people who begin with very little and risk everything to build successful careers in music. 
 The drama also brings together an acclaimed creative team. Writer Noh Hee-kyung , known for Our Blues  and Dear My Friends , reunites with director Lee Yoon-jung , whose previous work includes Coffee Prince  and Cheese in the Trap . 
 Here is everything to know about Tantara , including its release date, cast, plot, and streaming details! 
 Tantara Official Poster (Netflix) What Is Tantara About? 
 Set against the changing South Korean entertainment industry of the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s, Tantara  follows people who are determined to turn their difficult circumstances into something better. 
 Song Hye-kyo plays Min-ja, a woman whose challenging childhood shapes her strong will. When she sees an opportunity in the music business, she pursues it with determination, hoping to build a future beyond the hardships she has known. 
 Gong Yoo plays Dong-gu, Min-ja's childhood friend. The two have experienced difficult times together, and their bond remains important as they enter the entertainment industry. Although Dong-gu has an unpredictable personality, he listens to Min-ja and supports her as they chase their ambitions. 
 Tantara  (Netflix) Their journey brings them into contact with Min-hui ( Kim Seol-hyun ), an aspiring performer who shares a complicated relationship with Min-ja. Their bond is shaped by affection, resentment, and competing ambitions, adding another layer to the drama. 
 The story also features Gil-yeo ( Cha Seung-won ), a celebrated composer with a reputation for turning singers into stars, and Yang-ja ( Lee Ha-nee ), Min-hui's mother, who still hopes to become a singer herself. 
 With characters chasing success from different positions in the industry, Tantara  explores the sacrifices and difficult choices that can accompany a dream of fame. 
 Tantara Cast: Song Hye-kyo, Gong Yoo and More 
 One of the biggest attractions of Tantara  is its ensemble cast, bringing together established Korean stars across a story about ambition, music, and complicated relationships. 
 Song Hye-kyo as Min-ja 
 Following her acclaimed performance in The Glory , Song Hye-kyo takes on a period role as Min-ja, a determined woman who refuses to let her difficult upbringing decide her future. 
 Her character enters the music industry in search of new opportunities. The role gives Song another chance to portray a woman whose strength is shaped by hardship rather than an easy path to success. 
 Gong Yoo as Dong-gu 
 Gong Yoo plays Dong-gu, Min-ja's childhood friend who joins her in the entertainment business. Their shared history gives the relationship a foundation that predates their ambitions. 
 Known internationally for Goblin  and The Trunk , Gong Yoo reunites with director Lee Yoon-jung, who previously directed him in Coffee Prince . His role in Tantara  offers viewers a different setting from his recent thriller and fantasy projects. 
 Tantara  (Netflix) Kim Seol-hyun as Min-hui 
 Kim Seol-hyun plays Min-hui, an ambitious woman whose relationship with Min-ja is complicated by their shared history. She follows Min-ja's lead at times but also has a rebellious side and her own ideas about what she wants. 
 Her character adds tension to a story in which personal relationships and professional ambitions are closely connected. 
 Cha Seung-won as Gil-yeo 
 Cha Seung-won portrays Gil-yeo, a highly respected composer in the music industry. His reputation for helping singers achieve success makes him an influential figure in the world the younger characters are trying to enter. 
 Lee Ha-nee as Yang-ja 
 Lee Ha-nee plays Yang-ja, Min-hui's mother, who continues to dream of becoming a singer despite the difficulties she faces. Her storyline introduces another generation of people hoping to find a place in the entertainment industry. 
 The drama also features veteran actress Na Moon-hee as Mal-sun, adding further depth to the ensemble. 
 Why Tantara Is One of Netflix's K-Dramas to Watch in 2026 
 1. Song Hye-kyo and Gong Yoo Are Finally Sharing the Screen 
 Song Hye-kyo and Gong Yoo are two of South Korea's most recognizable actors, but their pairing in Tantara  gives audiences a new on-screen combination to look forward to. 
 Song has drawn international attention through dramas such as Descendants of the Sun  and The Glory , while Gong is widely recognized for Goblin , Train to Busan , and The Trunk . Their new project places them in a story that stretches beyond a conventional romance. 
 Their characters' childhood friendship and shared pursuit of success give the drama an emotional foundation, while the period setting creates a different backdrop for their relationship. 
 2. It Explores the Less Glamorous Side of Show Business 
 Stories about the entertainment industry can easily focus on fame, luxury, and celebrity life. Tantara  begins much earlier in its characters' journeys, when success is still a distant possibility. 
 Tantara  (Netflix) The series follows people who have little to rely on apart from their determination and willingness to take risks. Their ambitions bring them into a competitive world where talent alone may not be enough. 
 This focus on the struggle behind success could make Tantara  appealing to viewers who enjoy character-driven dramas about people trying to change their lives. 
 3. The Period Setting Spans Several Decades 
 By setting its story between the 1960s and 1980s, Tantara  has room to explore how the Korean entertainment industry changes over time. 
 The characters are not simply trying to become successful singers or industry figures. They are also navigating the expectations and limitations of the world around them. 
 The decades-long setting gives the story a wider scope, allowing personal ambitions and relationships to develop alongside a changing cultural landscape. 
 4. The Creative Team Has an Impressive Track Record 
 Noh Hee-kyung , the writer behind Our Blues  and Dear My Friends , is known for character-focused storytelling. Director Lee Yoon-jung has worked on popular dramas including Coffee Prince  and Cheese in the Trap . 
 Tantara  (Netflix) Their collaboration gives Tantara  an interesting combination of emotional storytelling and a period entertainment-industry setting. The series will bring together a large cast of characters whose ambitions and relationships are likely to shape the central conflict. 
 Whether the drama becomes a new favourite remains to be seen, but its creative team gives viewers a strong reason to keep it on their watchlists. 
 When Will Tantara Premiere on Netflix? 
 Tantara  will premiere globally on Netflix on December 11, 2026 . The platform announced the date alongside a new poster introducing the drama's characters and their journey through the music business. 
 The series is listed as a 2026 Netflix Korean drama, with 22 episodes reported by streaming sources so far. 
 Where to Watch Tantara 
 Tantara  will be available on Netflix worldwide from December 11, 2026 . Viewers will be able to follow Min-ja, Dong-gu, and the other characters as they pursue their ambitions in South Korea's music industry. 
 With Song Hye-kyo and Gong Yoo leading the cast, a story spanning several decades, and a creative team behind well-known Korean dramas, Tantara  is shaping up to be one of Netflix's major Korean drama releases to watch this December. 
 Are you excited to see Song Hye-kyo and Gong Yoo together in Tantara, or are you more interested in its story about South Korea's music industry?
